title: Iran Players Receive US Visas — 14 Officials Denied; Federation Accuses US of 'Vindictive Behavior'; Squad Departs Antalya for Tijuana; 5 Days to Group G Opener
detail: In the most consequential development of Iran's months-long World Cup visa crisis, the White House confirmed on June 6 that Iran's players and core athletic staff have received US visas — clearing the squad to enter the United States for their Group G matches. However, 14 key backroom staff and officials were denied entry, including secretary-general Hedayat Mombeini and vice president Mehdi Mohammad Nabi, prompting Iran's Football Federation to accuse the United States of 'vindictive behavior.' US Secretary of State Marco Rubio maintained that the concern was specifically with individuals with alleged ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), stating the process had been completed for athletes and support staff without such connections. Iran's squad departed their 15-day training camp in Antalya, Turkey at 6:30 PM local time on June 6, boarding a charter flight for Tijuana, Mexico with a brief stopover in Spain. Iran will base at Centro Xoloitzcuintle in Tijuana and commute across the US-Mexico border for their Group G matches at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California (June 15 vs New Zealand; June 21 vs Belgium) and Lumen Field in Seattle (June 26 vs Egypt). The visa approval for players — coming 10 days before their opening match — ends the most acute phase of the crisis, though the denial of 14 officials creates a significant operational challenge. Iran's federation president Mehdi Taj had submitted passports to the US Embassy in Ankara on June 5 and warned FIFA that denial would mean 'reconsideration of participation.' The approval averts what would have been an unprecedented World Cup forfeiture. 5 days to kickoff at Estadio Azteca.

title: Germany 2-1 USA at Soldier Field, Chicago — Final Pre-Tournament Warm-Up; Havertz 2', Sané 60'; USMNT Fall in Last Friendly Before Group D Opener
detail: Germany defeated the host nation United States 2-1 in their final pre-tournament friendly at Soldier Field in Chicago on June 6, delivering a sharp competitive test ahead of the World Cup opening on June 11. Kai Havertz struck in the 2nd minute to give Julian Nagelsmann's side the early initiative. The USA equalized through a Robinson goal before Leroy Sané restored Germany's lead around the 60th minute to seal the 2-1 win. The result will provide Germany — in Group E vs Curaçao, Ivory Coast, and Ecuador — with a confidence boost after their preparation period, while the USMNT heads into their June 12 Group D opener vs Paraguay (SoFi Stadium, LA) having now lost their final warm-up to a top-class European side. Nagelsmann's Germany side features Manuel Neuer (40) as first-choice goalkeeper and key attacking threats in Jamal Musiala and Florian Wirtz. USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino emphasized that the friendly result is irrelevant to tournament preparation — the coaching staff prioritized fitness and squad rotation over the result. Christian Pulisic, who captains the USMNT and broke his five-month scoring drought against Senegal on May 31, featured in the game alongside key squad members. 5 days to World Cup kickoff at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: Germany 2-1 USA at Soldier Field, Chicago — Havertz 2', Sané 60' defeat host nation in final pre-tournament tune-up

title: England 1-0 New Zealand (Kane Header); Belgium 5-0 Tunisia; Portugal 2-1 Chile (Leão Red Card) — Pre-Tournament Friendlies June 6
detail: Three further pre-tournament friendlies on June 6 provided final competitive tuneups. England defeated New Zealand 1-0 — Harry Kane converted a header in first-half stoppage time for Thomas Tuchel's side, a welcome pre-tournament marker for the captain who equalled Billy Wright's record of three World Cup captaincies. England are in Group L vs Croatia, Ghana, and Panama. Belgium hammered Tunisia 5-0 in comprehensive fashion as they gear up for Group G (with Iran, New Zealand, and Egypt) — the rout highlighted Belgium's attacking firepower ahead of the tournament proper. Portugal beat Chile 2-1, but the result was overshadowed by a Rafael Leão red card after a late altercation that leaves the AC Milan winger facing potential suspension for their June 18 Group K opener vs DR Congo. Roberto Martínez will assess the card's consequences with UEFA as Portugal count on Leão alongside the record-setting Cristiano Ronaldo (41, sixth World Cup) in their attacking lineup. 5 days to World Cup kickoff at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: Harry Kane heads England to 1-0 win over New Zealand — Belgium thrash Tunisia 5-0; Portugal edge Chile 2-1 (Leão red card)

title: Argentina's Balerdi Ruled Out of World Cup With Soleus Injury — Senesi Leading Replacement Candidate; Emiliano Martínez Remains Despite Fractured Finger
detail: Argentina suffered a significant defensive blow on June 6 when centre-back Leonardo Balerdi was ruled out of the 2026 World Cup with a soleus muscle injury to his right leg, sustained during the squad's training camp. Coach Lionel Scaloni confirmed the exclusion and indicated that Bournemouth's Marcos Senesi is the leading candidate for the replacement slot under FIFA's medical exception rules, with a final decision expected shortly. The loss of Balerdi is an added defensive headache for Scaloni, who is already managing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez's fractured ring finger on his right hand — sustained during the Europa League final with Aston Villa vs Freiburg. Martínez remains in the squad and is expected to play. Messi himself has been managing a left hamstring concern after a 'muscular overload' in late May but is expected to be available for Argentina's Group J opener vs Algeria on June 16 at Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City. The defending champions remain pre-tournament title favorites despite the injury concerns, with 17 returners from the 2022 World Cup squad. 5 days to kickoff at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: Leonardo Balerdi ruled out of World Cup 2026 — Argentina's defensive setup hit by soleus injury; Senesi leads replacement candidates
